title: Types of data: categorical, numerical, etc

cues.en: Mike: This is a pretty foundational lecture in the sense that the concepts and the terms that I'm going to introduce you to in this video will appear multiple times
cues.zh: 這是相當基礎的一堂講座，因為這部影片介紹的概念與術語，會多次出現在，

cues.en: throughout this course and also throughout your adventures in the land of statistics.
cues.zh: 整門課，以及你探索統計世界的過程中。

cues.en: So, let's begin.
cues.zh: 開始吧。

cues.en: So the point of this video is to introduce you to data types.
cues.zh: 這部影片的重點，是介紹資料類型。

cues.en: So what are data types?
cues.zh: 什麼是資料類型？

cues.en: Well, to start with, I already need to give you a bit of a disambiguation, and that is the difference between data type in computer science and data type in statistics.
cues.zh: 一開始就得先釐清一點，也就是電腦科學中的資料型別，與統計中的資料類型，有何不同。

cues.en: Now, something that plagues science in general in human civilization is inconsistent and annoying terminology.
cues.zh: 整個人類文明的科學，一直受到不一致又惱人的術語困擾。

cues.en: So this is not just something in statistics.
cues.zh: 這不只發生在統計。

cues.en: You'll see in math and physics and biology and computer science and economics, different people use different terms for the same concept
cues.zh: 數學、物理、生物、電腦科學、經濟學中，都會看到不同人，用不同詞彙表示同一概念，

cues.en: and different people use the same terms for different concepts, it's really annoying.
cues.zh: 也會用相同詞彙表示不同概念，真的很惱人。

cues.en: And in statistics, the terminology, the terminological confusion is particularly deleterious because so many branches, so many distinct branches
cues.zh: 在統計中，這種術語混淆特別有害，因為科學中有那麼多不同分支，

cues.en: of science use statistics.
cues.zh: 都會使用統計。

cues.en: So whether you are coming from an engineering background or a data science background, a psychology or biology background, whatever your background is,
cues.zh: 所以不論來自工程、資料科學、心理學或生物學背景，無論什麼背景，

cues.en: you might actually be using different terms from other people who come from different backgrounds, even though you're talking about the same thing.
cues.zh: 即使談的是同一件事，實際用的術語，也可能和不同背景的人不一樣。

cues.en: So there isn't much that can be done about this except to be patient and accept that although terminological ambiguity is not really very nice,
cues.zh: 對這件事沒什麼辦法，只能耐心接受。雖然術語歧義並不好，

cues.en: it's not good for cross-collaborations, it's not good for progress and science, but that's just the world we live in.
cues.zh: 不利於跨領域合作，也不利於進步與科學，但我們生活的世界就是這樣。

cues.en: All right, so with that rant aside, let me now explain the difference between data type in computer science and data type in statistics.
cues.zh: 先把抱怨放一邊，現在說明電腦科學資料型別，與統計資料類型的差別。

cues.en: Here we are talking about the category of data, and here, when computer science data type refers to the format of data storage, the implications of different data types here
cues.zh: 統計這裡談的是資料的分類；電腦科學的資料型別，則指資料儲存格式。不同型別的影響在於，

cues.en: are for the kinds of operations that can be done on different variables, how much space different kinds of variables, different data types take up in your,
cues.zh: 不同變數能做哪些運算，各種變數、資料型別，在，

cues.en: in the computer's memory, and data type in statistics has applications for which kinds of statistical procedures can be performed, as well as what kinds of visualizations
cues.zh: 電腦記憶體中占多少空間。而統計資料類型，影響能進行哪些統計程序，以及哪些視覺化，

cues.en: are most appropriate.
cues.zh: 最適合。

cues.en: So here are a few examples.
cues.zh: 舉幾個例子。

cues.en: You can have data be floating point or Boolean or string or character or function or class.
cues.zh: 資料可以是浮點數、布林值、字串、字元、函式或類別。

cues.en: There's lots of different types of data in computer science, and sometimes there is a bit of a mapping between the computer science data type
cues.zh: 電腦科學有很多不同資料型別，有時它們和，

cues.en: and the statistics data type, but not really, that's not generally the case.
cues.zh: 統計資料類型稍有對應，但其實大多不是這樣。

cues.en: All right, so with that said, now let me introduce you to the, to some different data types in statistics.
cues.zh: 說明完之後，現在介紹統計中一些不同資料類型。

cues.en: Now there are many different data types that people have distinguished in statistics.
cues.zh: 人們在統計中區分了許多不同類型。

cues.en: This is a non-exhaustive list that I took from Wikipedia, and if you look through stats textbooks, then you might find even more
cues.zh: 這是我從 Wikipedia 取得的不完整清單。查看統計教科書，可能找到更多，

cues.en: or differently labeled types of data.
cues.zh: 或名稱不同的資料類型。

cues.en: All right, so in this course I'm going to distinguish between five different types of data that are broadly fit into two categories.
cues.zh: 這門課，我會區分五種資料類型，大致歸成兩大類。

cues.en: So I do not mean to suggest that these are the only or like the best five types of data, but these are the types of data that come up most often, certainly in this course,
cues.zh: 不是說只有這五種，或它們最好，但至少在本課程中，這些最常出現，

cues.en: and I think also in general in modern statistics.
cues.zh: 我想在一般現代統計中也是如此。

cues.en: Okay, so we start off with the numerical category or which is describing numbers.
cues.zh: 先從數值類別開始，也就是描述數字。

cues.en: So our first example will be, our first type will be what's called interval type data.
cues.zh: 第一個例子、第一種類型，叫做區間資料。

cues.en: Interval data have a numeric scale with meaningful intervals and arbitrary precision.
cues.zh: 區間資料有數值尺度，間隔具有意義，而且精度可任意細分。

cues.en: So one example is temperature in Celsius.
cues.zh: 一個例子是攝氏溫度。

cues.en: So what does arbitrary precision mean?
cues.zh: 什麼叫精度可任意細分？

cues.en: I actually didn't write that here, but you'll see it come up later.
cues.zh: 我這裡其實沒寫，但稍後會看到。

cues.en: Well, we can measure the temperature outside.
cues.zh: 我們可以測量室外溫度。

cues.en: Let's say it's 24 degrees Celsius, which is a really perfect temperature.
cues.zh: 假設是攝氏 24 度，這是非常完美的溫度。

cues.en: If you had a really precise thermometer, you wouldn't see that it's exactly 24 degrees.
cues.zh: 如果溫度計非常精準，就不會看到剛好 24 度。

cues.en: It's probably, it could be 24.12 Celsius.
cues.zh: 可能是攝氏 24.12 度。

cues.en: And if you had an even more precise thermometer, then you might find the temperature to be 24.12076, whatever.
cues.zh: 如果溫度計更精準，可能測到 24.12076 度之類。

cues.en: So the better your instrument gets, the better your measurement sensor, the more precise you can be in terms of this measurement.
cues.zh: 所以儀器越好、測量感測器越好，測量值就能越精細。

cues.en: So this is referring to interval.
cues.zh: 這就是區間資料。

cues.en: On the other hand, zero degrees celsius does not mean the absence of temperature.
cues.zh: 另一方面，攝氏 0 度，並不代表沒有溫度。

cues.en: It doesn't mean that there's no temperature.
cues.zh: 不代表完全沒有溫度。

cues.en: And that's when we switch to what's called a ratio scale.
cues.zh: 這就帶到所謂的比率尺度。

cues.en: So a ratio scale is basically like an interval.
cues.zh: 比率尺度基本上類似區間尺度。

cues.en: We have arbitrary precision, we have meaningful intervals, but we also have a meaningful zero which we don't have with interval data.
cues.zh: 精度可任意細分，間隔有意義，但還多了有意義的零點，這是區間資料沒有的。

cues.en: So one example is height in centimeters.
cues.zh: 一個例子是以公分表示的身高。

cues.en: If you are zero centimeters tall, well I guess you wouldn't be, but you can imagine that zero centimeters tall really does correspond to the absence of height.
cues.zh: 如果身高是 0 公分，嗯，大概不會有人是這樣，但可以想像，0 公分確實對應完全沒有高度。

cues.en: Another example would be money.
cues.zh: 另一個例子是錢。

cues.en: If you have zero euros then you have no money, unfortunately, I hope you're doing okay if that's the case.
cues.zh: 如果有 0 歐元，就沒有錢了。很不幸，如果真是這樣，希望你還好。

cues.en: And then we have the third type of numerical data and that is called discreet data.
cues.zh: 第三種數值資料，叫做離散資料。

cues.en: So here we have basically just integer.
cues.zh: 基本上就是整數。

cues.en: So there's meaningful numbers, but there's no arbitrary precision, we just have integers.
cues.zh: 數字有意義，但不能任意細分精度，只有整數。

cues.en: One example is the population.
cues.zh: 一個例子是人口。

cues.en: So the population of the Netherlands is, I don't know exactly, but it's around 18 million.
cues.zh: 荷蘭人口，我不確定精確數字，但大約一千八百萬。

cues.en: Now the population is going to be some integer number.
cues.zh: 人口會是某個整數。

cues.en: It's not 18.3 million people, it's just 18 million.
cues.zh: 不是一千八百三十萬人，而是一千八百萬。

cues.en: So these are the three types of numerical data.
cues.zh: 這是三種數值資料。

cues.en: And I'm gonna talk about, we'll see some examples on the next slide, and you will learn more about these distinctions and the definitions in the next several videos
cues.zh: 下一張投影片會看一些例子，接下來幾部影片，還會更深入學習這些區別與定義，

cues.en: and also over the next, over the rest of this course.
cues.zh: 以及本課程剩下的部分。

cues.en: Okay, so now we move from numerical to categorical data, which is also sometimes called label data.
cues.zh: 現在從數值資料，轉到類別資料，有時也叫標籤資料。

cues.en: And in general these are data that either don't really have a specific number assigned to them or the numbers are not as meaningful, their intervals are not as meaningful
cues.zh: 一般而言，這些資料不是沒有指定特定數值，就是數值與間隔的意義，

cues.en: as they're with these types of data.
cues.zh: 不如前面那些資料。

cues.en: So we have two different types of categorical data.
cues.zh: 類別資料分成兩種。

cues.en: One is ordinal, and that's when the data are, or the categories are sortable, but they're also discreet.
cues.zh: 一種是次序資料，也就是資料或類別可以排序，但同時也是離散的。

cues.en: So one example would be the level of education.
cues.zh: 例如教育程度。

cues.en: So imagine you are doing a survey or you have a website and you're asking someone to fill in their highest level of education.
cues.zh: 想像你做問卷，或在網站上，請某人填寫最高學歷。

cues.en: So we have middle school, high school, university, bachelor's, master's and PhDs, that was five.
cues.zh: 有國中、高中、大學學士、碩士與博士，共五個。

cues.en: Now those are discreet categories, but they are sortable.
cues.zh: 這些是離散類別，但可以排序。

cues.en: So we can sort the level of education.
cues.zh: 所以能排序教育程度。

cues.en: So a bachelor's degree is beyond a high school degree and a master's degree is beyond a bachelor's degree.
cues.zh: 學士學位高於高中學歷，碩士學位又高於學士。

cues.en: Now the key difference between ordinal and discreet is that with ordinal data, the differences are not necessarily all meaningful
cues.zh: 次序資料與離散資料的關鍵差別，是次序資料之間的差異，不一定全都具有，

cues.en: in the same way.
cues.zh: 相同的意義。

cues.en: So the difference between high school and bachelor's is not the same thing as the difference between bachelor's and master's.
cues.zh: 高中與學士之間的差異，不等於學士與碩士之間的差異。

cues.en: And that's not the same thing as the difference between masters and PhD and so on.
cues.zh: 也不等於碩士與博士之間的差異，依此類推。

cues.en: So we do have a way to sort them, but we don't have a meaningful constant interval relationship between the different levels.
cues.zh: 所以有方法排序，但不同層級之間，沒有有意義且固定的間隔關係。

cues.en: So that's ordinal data.
cues.zh: 這就是次序資料。

cues.en: And then finally we have nominal data.
cues.zh: 最後是名目資料。

cues.en: And these are discreet, like ordinal, but they're non-sortable.
cues.zh: 和次序資料一樣是離散的，但無法排序。

cues.en: So let's imagine we have another survey.
cues.zh: 想像另一份問卷。

cues.en: We're asking people to report the genre of movie that they most recently watched.
cues.zh: 請人們回報最近看過的電影類型。

cues.en: So we can have, there's sci-fi movies, that's one genre.
cues.zh: 例如科幻片，這是一種類型。

cues.en: And this thing, which I admit that I only recently learned this term, it's rom-com, for romantic comedy, you can tell which kinds of movies I generally don't spend a lot of time watching.
cues.zh: 還有這個詞，我承認最近才學到，rom-com，代表浪漫喜劇。你應該看得出，我平常不太花時間看哪類電影。

cues.en: Now you can ask someone to rate movies according to their preferences, but in general, the different genres of movies
cues.zh: 可以請人們依偏好為電影評分，但一般而言，不同電影類型，

cues.en: are not intrinsically sortable.
cues.zh: 本質上無法排序。

cues.en: You can't say that sci-fi is greater than rom-com, which is greater than just a regular drama.
cues.zh: 不能說科幻大於浪漫喜劇，又大於一般劇情片。

cues.en: And like with ordinal data, there's no interval or ratio relationship between these.
cues.zh: 而且和次序資料一樣，它們之間沒有區間或比率關係。

cues.en: So you can't say that sci-fi equals two times rom-com.
cues.zh: 不能說科幻等於兩倍的浪漫喜劇。

cues.en: That that doesn't even make any sense.
cues.zh: 那根本沒有意義。

cues.en: So these are discreet categories, they have labels and they are non-sortable.
cues.zh: 所以這些是離散、有標籤，而且無法排序的類別。

cues.en: So those are called nominal data.
cues.zh: 這些就叫名目資料。

cues.en: All right, so this is a brief explanation, and what I have on this slide is several different examples.
cues.zh: 以上是簡短說明。這張投影片上有幾個不同例子。

cues.en: And what I want you to do is pause the video and come up with the label from, so the data type from the previous slide,
cues.zh: 我要你暫停影片，從前一張投影片找出你認為，

cues.en: that you think best fits each one of these individual items, each of these explanations of data type.
cues.zh: 最適合每個個別項目，也就是這些資料描述的類型。

cues.en: All right, did you do it yet? So here are my answers.
cues.zh: 做完了嗎？這是我的答案。

cues.en: The number of widgets purchased in a particular month.
cues.zh: 某個月份購買的小物件數量。

cues.en: I'm assuming that widgets are concrete things.
cues.zh: 我假設小物件是實體物品。

cues.en: So you just have one or two or five widgets.
cues.zh: 所以就是一個、兩個或五個。

cues.en: So I'm calling that discreet.
cues.zh: 我把它歸為離散資料。

cues.en: It's numeric, but it doesn't have arbitrary precision, there's just an integer number of these.
cues.zh: 它是數值，但精度不能任意細分，數量只能是整數。

cues.en: Okay, so then we have the last three countries visited, something you might get asked about, when entering into a country.
cues.zh: 接著，最近造訪的三個國家。入境時，可能會被問到這個問題。

cues.en: These are nominal data because they're not sorted.
cues.zh: 這是名目資料，因為沒有排序。

cues.en: However, if you would ask someone to identify their three favorite countries sorted in order of their favoriteness, maybe someone says Vietnam, Fiji, New Zealand,
cues.zh: 但如果請某人，依喜好列出最喜歡的三個國家，也許他說越南、斐濟、紐西蘭，

cues.en: all roughly in kind of the same corner of the world.
cues.zh: 大致都在世界的同一個角落。

cues.en: Now all of a sudden we switch to ordinal data because for that one individual, these data actually are sorted.
cues.zh: 這時突然就變成次序資料，因為對這個人而言，資料確實經過排序。

cues.en: Now these are ordinal because the difference between Vietnam and Fiji in terms of preference is not the same thing as the difference between Fiji and New Zealand.
cues.zh: 它是次序資料，因為偏好上，越南與斐濟的差異，不等於斐濟與紐西蘭的差異。

cues.en: So there isn't like a ratio order or meaningful ratio between these different items.
cues.zh: 所以這些項目之間，沒有比率順序或有意義的比率。

cues.en: And the reason why I include these two problems here is so you can see that sometimes in statistics, the correct answer or the correct analysis,
cues.zh: 我放這兩題，是讓你看到，在統計中，正確答案、正確分析，

cues.en: the correct visualization, the right thing to do, is not necessarily intrinsic to the data itself.
cues.zh: 正確視覺化、正確做法，不一定由資料本身決定。

cues.en: It can be related to the way that you phrase the question, the kind of hypothesis you're asking, and that's one of the things
cues.zh: 也可能與問題怎麼措辭、提出哪種假設有關，這也是，

cues.en: that makes statistics more challenging than mathematics, because you have some ambiguity that's built into it.
cues.zh: 統計比數學更具挑戰的原因之一，因為裡面本來就有一些歧義。

cues.en: So let's see, we have gender, that's nominal, the land area of forests, that's ratio, because it is meaningful to have zero land area of forest.
cues.zh: 接著，性別是名目資料；森林土地面積是比率資料，因為森林面積為零有意義。

cues.en: You can imagine a desert has zero land area of forest, so there's no forest there.
cues.zh: 可以想像沙漠的森林面積是零，也就是沒有森林。

cues.en: Then we have cities sorted by population, I call that ordinal.
cues.zh: 接著，依人口排序的城市，我稱為次序資料。

cues.en: Again, this depends, the correct answer here depends on the kind of question you are asking, because if you want to know the population itself,
cues.zh: 同樣，正確答案取決於問的是哪種問題。如果想知道人口本身，

cues.en: that would be discreet data.
cues.zh: 那就是離散資料。

cues.en: But if you're sorting cities according to their population, then you have ordinal data.
cues.zh: 但如果根據人口排序城市，就是次序資料。

cues.en: So these are sortable, but the relationship, the population ratio between Beijing to New York is not the same thing as the relationship,
cues.zh: 它們可以排序，但北京與紐約之間的人口比率關係，與，

cues.en: the ratio of population between New York and Villa Las Estrellas.
cues.zh: 紐約和 Villa Las Estrellas 之間的人口比率，不是同一回事。

cues.en: And if you don't know where this city is, it's pretty neat.
cues.zh: 如果不知道這座城在哪裡，它相當有意思。

cues.en: You can spend some time looking it up after the video.
cues.zh: 影片結束後，可以花點時間查查。

cues.en: Okay, so then we have interval, I accidentally already mentioned this example in the previous slide, so maybe you got that one for free.
cues.zh: 接著是區間資料。我在前一張投影片不小心已經提過這個例子，所以這題可能白送你了。

cues.en: And then finally we have satisfaction with this course so far, I hope it's closer to 5 than to 1.
cues.zh: 最後，是你目前對這門課的滿意度。希望比較接近 5，而不是 1。

cues.en: And again, these are ordinal data because the difference between rating this course a 1 and a 2 is not the same thing
cues.zh: 這同樣是次序資料，因為把課程評為 1 和 2 的差異，

cues.en: as the difference in rating between 4 and 5.
cues.zh: 不等於評為 4 和 5 的差異。

cues.en: So that's why these are ordinal data and not ratio or interval data.
cues.zh: 所以是次序資料，而非比率或區間資料。

cues.en: All right, so why do these data types matter?
cues.zh: 這些資料類型為什麼重要？

cues.en: Well, they matter because some statistical analyses can be applied only to certain data types.
cues.zh: 因為有些統計分析，只能用於特定資料類型。

cues.en: And you'll see several examples of this as we go through the course.
cues.zh: 接下來的課程，會看到好幾個例子。

cues.en: Likewise, there are certain visualization methods that are valid for some types of data and not valid or not appropriate for other types of data.
cues.zh: 同樣，有些視覺化方法對某類資料有效，對其他類型則無效或不適合。

cues.en: So it is important to know what the general data type is that you're working with.
cues.zh: 所以知道自己處理的資料大致屬於哪種類型，很重要。

cues.en: Now that said, is this the sort of thing that you should memorize?
cues.zh: 不過，這需要背嗎？

cues.en: Should you memorize the the names of these data types?
cues.zh: 應該記住這些資料類型的名稱嗎？

cues.en: I don't know, if you need this, if you're taking this course to help you study for an exam, then yeah, this might be an exam.
cues.zh: 我不知道。如果上這門課是為了準備考試，那是的，這可能會考。

cues.en: Otherwise, I don't know if you really need to memorize all of these names, however, it is important for you to understand the different kinds of data, the different characteristics of data,
cues.zh: 否則，我不知道是否真的需要記住所有名稱，但理解不同類型與特性，很重要，

cues.en: numerical and categorical and so on.
cues.zh: 例如數值、類別等等。

cues.en: I do have to admit that when I was creating this course, when I was making these slides, I forgot about the names.
cues.zh: 我得承認，製作課程、做這些投影片時，我忘記了名稱。

cues.en: I had to look up the names, although I do remember the ideas of, I remember the properties, but I forgot the data names.
cues.zh: 我必須查名稱。雖然記得概念與性質，卻忘了資料類型的名字。

cues.en: So I don't know.
cues.zh: 所以我不知道。

cues.en: I'm reluctant to tell you that you need to memorize this table that I showed you a few slides ago.
cues.zh: 我不太願意告訴你，一定要背下前幾張投影片上的表格。

cues.en: Anyway, I hope you found this lecture interesting and insightful.
cues.zh: 總之，希望你覺得這堂課有趣而且有啟發。

cues.en: It is important to understand the characteristics, the features of different types of data because those will constrain the kinds of analyses
cues.zh: 理解不同資料類型的性質與特徵很重要，因為它們會限制你能對資料做哪些分析，

cues.en: and visualizations that you are able to do on your data.
cues.zh: 以及視覺化。
